newsitem.title: LATVIA: TALINVEST GETS OK TO TRADE LATVIAN SHARES.
newsitem.headline: TALINVEST GETS OK TO TRADE LATVIAN SHARES.

text.p: Investment house Talinvest said on Wednesday that it has gained a licence to trade Latvian shares.
Talinvest director Richard Svelpe told Reuters that Talinvest became a Riga bourse shareholder in December and has now got permission to trade shares.
"We were granted a licence to buy and sell and to be an account keeper in Riga," Svelpe said.

Talinvest broker Roland Klincis said that the firm's main clients were foreign investors and that interest in Latvian shares has increased since the country got an investment-grade credit rating from Standard & Poor's.
"We are now going to buy and sell equities on the Riga stock exchange on behalf of our clients which are mainly non-residents, that is, foreign capital," Klincis said.
"We have noticed that interest has increased after the credit rating," he added.
Talinvest recently bought a stake in Lithuania broker Suprema and so is now present in all three Baltic markets.
